subject: Private deployment maintenance window proposal & rollback authority
messages:
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Steve Holmes <steve.holmes@aerohealth.com>, itops@aerohealth.com
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 07 Jun 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment maintenance window proposal & rollback authority

Hi Steve / AeroHealth ops,

Following our runbook review last week, we need to schedule the version rollout for your private VPC (customer pin currently on v1.8.2). Proposed window: Sunday Jun 15 02:00-06:00 PT (low traffic + time zone overlap with your on-call). Key asks up front:

- Customer sign-off on the proposed window and canary criteria.
- Agreement on the pinning policy: we propose keeping customer pinned to v1.8.2 for 72 hours post-canary if no regressions, then unpin to allow auto-upgrades.
- Authorization for the ops on-call to execute emergency rollback (full pin reapply) if canary failure meets abort criteria.

Attached: 20250607_rollout_plan.pdf (full step-by-step), rollback_checklist.md (quick abort steps), canary_metrics_template.csv (what we'll monitor).

Short summary of tech steps (full details in attachment):
1) Preflight: snapshot KV cache, export metrics, confirm backups of indexed storage.
2) Canary: 2 nodes in the dedicated pool, 6-hour canary, traffic split 5% -> new binary (v1.9.0-rc2).
3) Gradual ramp: if canary passes, roll to remaining nodes in 3 waves over 2 hours.
4) Post-mortem window: 72 hours watch before unpin.

Monica will own the runbook for the rollout and Soojin will own the emergency rollback path. Marissa will coordinate communications and post-rollout telemetry.

Please reply with ACCEPT / DECLINE / NEEDS CHANGES and any specific timing constraints by Tue Jun 10 COB.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20250607_rollout_plan.pdf (18 pages), rollback_checklist.md (2 pages), canary_metrics_template.csv (CSV)
From: Steve Holmes <steve.holmes@aerohealth.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, itops@aerohealth.com
Date: Sun, 08 Jun 2025 09:46:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance window proposal & rollback authority

Kimberly,

Thanks for the clear plan and attachments — the team here reviewed them this morning. A few clarifications before we sign off:

- Pinning: AeroHealth prefers a 7-day pin for major behavioral changes due to regulatory reporting dependencies. Is 72 hours adjustable to 7 days if the canary passes?
- Canary traffic: can we extend the canary to 12 hours? Our peak query types for billing reconciliation run overnight ET, so a longer canary reduces risk.
- Rollback timing: if a rollback is triggered, we need a confirmation cadence and a named contact at Redwood who can authorize the final failback (we require an engineer on-call plus an SLAed approval).

We tentatively agree to the Jun 15 window pending answers above. Also: will rolling back re-instate the exact prior KV cache or do we expect a cold-start pain for stateful routes? That has downstream impact on our ingestion pipeline.

Steve Holmes
Director, Platform Engineering
AeroHealth

--
AeroHealth IT Ops: itops@aerohealth.com
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Steve Holmes <steve.holmes@aerohealth.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jun 2025 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance window proposal & rollback authority

Steve — thanks for the questions, good calls. Short answers, then a few operational details:

- Pin duration: we can accommodate a 7-day customer pin post-rollout for AeroHealth. Since we maintain the private control plane, we'll set an account-level pin for v1.9.0 with a 7-day TTL and monitor telemetry. If you want us to extend beyond 7 days we can add a calendar-based override.

- Canary length: agree to 12-hour canary (will make minor schedule adjustments). We'll run the canary from 02:00-14:00 PT to cover your overnight ET window.

- Rollback authority: Redwood requires a two-person action to execute a failback for private fleets — 1) Ops on-call engineer executes rollback steps, 2) an authorized product/ops manager provides explicit approval (email or DocuSign quick consent). For this rollout, Kimberly (ops manager) will be the named approver. We will log the approval in the change record.

- KV cache behavior: rollback re-applies the pinned model binary and restarts serving processes. We will rehydrate prefix/KV caches where possible from the preflight snapshot (we snapshot top-10% hot prefixes and persistent caches). Cold-starts are possible for some ephemeral routes; we estimate a 5-10 minute warm-up per node during heavy traffic. We'll include an ingest backpressure plan in the runbook to smooth downstream load.

Operational runbook highlights (excerpt):
* Preflight checklist (30m): health-checks, metrics baseline capture, datastore snapshot, confirm rollback artifacts.
* Canary (12h): 2-node canary, 5% traffic, automated SLO gates (latency P95<120ms, error rate <0.5%, inference quality regressions flagged by evals).
* Abort criteria: error rate >0.5% sustained for 3m OR latency P95 >250ms for 10m OR automated quality regression >3% across tracked prompts.
* Emergency rollback steps (fast path):
  1. Pause ingress routing to canary and drain.
  2. Reapply pin (v1.8.2) to entire fleet via control plane.
  3. Restart serving processes on nodes, rehydrate caches from snapshot.
  4. Validate health checks, then reopen traffic slowly.

I've attached the rollback_checklist.md and a canary metrics template for your ops to review. If AeroHealth agrees, we'll update the change record and Kimberly will finalize the DocuSign quick-approval stub for the two-person rollback authorization.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback_checklist.md, canary_metrics_template.csv
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment maintenance window proposal & rollback authority

Steve — appreciate the quick review and the request for extra safety. AeroHealth requests accepted:

- Pin set to 7 days post-successful rollout.
- Canary extended to 12 hours (02:00-14:00 PT) as Monica outlined.
- Rollback authorization: I will be the named approver; Ops on-call will execute. I'll also sign the DocuSign stub prior to the window and confirm contact info in the change record.

Marissa: please create the customer-facing comms (one-line summary + expected impact) and a rollback-ready status channel in PagerDuty + Slack. Soojin: please run the preflight snapshot play in staging tomorrow and confirm KV snapshot health. Monica: update the change record with the extended canary and the 7-day pin TTL.

Steve / AeroHealth IT: once you reply with ACCEPT we will mark the change record as scheduled for Jun 15 02:00 PT and send the DocuSign approval link.

Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
